stage_a.note: The founders maintain an incredibly upbeat, smiling, and energetic delivery throughout the entire presentation.
They show very strong excitement about the product, dancing and celebrating its use cases.
The mother and daughter interact with pronounced warmth, smiling at each other and the panel.

venture.description: A styling tool that easily applies adhesive crystals and gems to hair.
venture.note: A hand-held device that clicks gems onto hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, explain how the Blinger tool works, and demonstrate applying gems to hair.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: The founders hand out samples and wigs. The investors test the product on the wigs and on themselves.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how long they have been selling the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains it took four years to get a prototype, going through multiple engineering firms and accumulating debt.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much debt she took on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states she was in 1.7 million dollars of debt.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what she did next.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains she maxed out her debt, sold her house, and used the money to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies that she actually sold her house.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms she sold the house, rented a townhome, manufactured the product, and took it to a toy fair.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what happened at the toy fair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she scheduled pitches with toy companies and ended up getting a licensing deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks what royalty rate she received.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states she got 5% and they did over 20 million dollars wholesale in 2019.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what happened after that successful year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains that Covid happened and sales went down, dropping her income.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if she believes the royalties will continue to come in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says the situation was bad and implies the royalties dropped significantly.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori notes that 2020 happened, they expected a lot in 2021, and sales went far down.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains that legal infringers totally knocked off the product all over the internet when a celebrity used it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if the overall product category went up even though her specific sales were affected by knockoffs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she had started working because she kept the women's market as part of her licensing deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark confirms that she retained the rights to the women's market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms yes, she retained those rights and started selling it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what changed with the toy company and how she got the kids' rights back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains the toy company said it was knocked off everywhere and gave the rights back to her.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm that she now owns 100% of both the women's and kids' products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms that she owns everything today.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what her sales are today.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states they have 1,640,000 dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if those are this year's sales and if they are profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms that they are profitable.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how profitable they are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says they should finish with 1.5 million this year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark clarifies that she is stating sales, and asks what the profit is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states they should end at 4.2 million, confusing sales and profit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark and Robert clarify that she means sales will go from 1.7 million to 4.2 million by year end.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how much is in inventory and where the cash went.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says it is all in inventory.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much the inventory is worth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states the inventory is worth about 2.5 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what she plans to do with the 200,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she just wants one of them to partner with her, avoiding the specific use of funds.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks who else is helping her run the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie admits she has no business experience and relies on two ladies and her daughter to help her.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if she has a Chief Financial Officer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says they do not have a CFO and really need a bookkeeper.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how she keeps her books and knows if she is making money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie claims they know and try to put out fires first, but admits she needs help.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin exits, noting her massive inventory and lack of operational expertise.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating she needs someone to run operations and is not ready for an investor.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara offers $200k for 25% contingent on Angie coming to New York to organize her business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert exits, praising her as a dreamer but saying she is not an operator.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, advising Angie to take Barbara's offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie hesitates, expressing that 25% feels really high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie asks Barbara if she will fund purchase orders.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara revises her offer, maintaining 25% but adding that she will fund purchase orders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie accepts Barbara's revised offer.

decisions.note: She has massive inventory and lacks the operational expertise to run the business.
She needs an operator to run the business and is not in a position to take an investor.

decisions.terms: $200,000 for 25% contingent on coming to NY.
decisions.note: She believes in the founder's persistence but requires her to come to NY to organize the business.
He thinks she is an incredible dreamer but not a good operator.
She thinks Barbara's offer is great and advises the founder to take it.
She agrees to fund purchase orders as long as the founder has them, keeping equity at 25%.

record.notes: The founder briefly confuses sales and profit projections but is quickly corrected by the panel.
